pr_title: drivers: i2c_nrfx_twim: Fix write transaction issues
pr_body:
_drivers: i2c_nrfx_twim: Use concatenation buffer by default_

Issue an error logging message when the i2c_nrfx_twim driver lacks
a concatenation buffer big enough to properly handle a call to
i2c_burst_write() function, to give the user a hint what is wrong.

Also use by default a 16-bytes long concatenation buffer for every
instance of the i2c_nrfx_twim driver. Such value should cover most
of the simple uses of the i2c_burst_write() function, like those
in the stmemsc sensor drivers, and when a longer buffer is needed,
the user will be provided with the above message pointing to the
property that should be adjusted.

Fixes #33440.

_drivers: i2c_nrfx_twim: Add handling of buffers located in flash_

TWIM peripherals cannot perform write transactions from buffers
located in flash. The content of such buffers needs to be copied
to RAM before the actual transfer can be requested.
This commits adds a new property (zephyr,flash-buf-max-size) that
informs the driver how much space in RAM needs to be reserved for
such copying and adds proper handling of buffers located in flash.
This fixes an issue that caused that e.g. the DPS310 sensor driver
did not work on nRF SoCs that only have TWIM, not TWI peripherals.

Fixes #35550.

issue_context.title: nRF91: DPS310 I2C driver not working
comments:
> In the DPS310 driver `dps310_init()` function;
> The code runs as expected up to reading the product ID and then the `i2c_write_read()` call for reading calibration coefficients fails and gives a negative value for input/output error failing to initialize the driver properly.
> 
> ```
> I2C error: -5 
> ```
> 
> What is surprising that the I2C call for reading the product ID from the sensor register works and it gives the correct product id as `0x10h` which indicates that connections and i2c address are correct.
> 
> Looking deeper into the code, the ` i2c_reg_read_byte()` actually returns ` i2c_write_read()`. However, directly calling the ` i2c_write_read()` in the DPS310 driver layer is not working as expected. So why does one I2C API call works while the other does not?

I think the problem is that the TWIM peripheral that handles I2C in nRF9160 cannot perform a transaction when the provided buffer is located in flash, and that is the case when `i2c_write_read()` is called from the DPS310 driver (`REG_ADDR_CALIB_COEFF_0` is defined as `static const`). When `i2c_write_read()` is called via `i2c_reg_read_byte()`, the buffer to be sent is `&reg_addr`, so it will be on the stack, i.e. in RAM.
You can confirm this by trying to use the following in the driver:
```
	uint8_t raw_coef[18] = { 0 };
	uint8_t reg_addr = REG_ADDR_CALIB_COEFF_0;

	res = i2c_write_read(data->i2c_master, config->i2c_addr,
			     &reg_addr, 1, &raw_coef, 18);
```
But that's obviously not a proper solution of this problem. The i2c_nrfx_twim driver needs to be improved to handle also transfers from flash (use some internal buffer and copy there the provided data from flash to overcome the limitation of the TWIM peripheral).

@anangl,
Thanks for the suggestion. So after making similar changes (or should I say hack) across the DPS310 driver code, basically, getting rid of `static const uint8_t` especially for the register addresses and the buffer to be written, I have managed the driver to work and fetch the sensor values.
Now all the` i2c_write_read()` calls within this driver are working as expected without error values.
For now, I will make the changes to the DPS310 driver and use it as a local driver rather than directly fetching it from Zephyr's driver library.
Thanks and I hope in the future release this issue will be hopefully fixed for all the related drivers or the core i2c driver itself.
@anangl do you want to open an enhancement and close this?

> @anangl do you want to open an enhancement and close this?

@carlescufi I think it is fine to keep this issue open as a bug. This missing feature of the i2c_nrfx_twim driver actually causes the DPS310 driver to not work on nRF9160, so that's something that needs to be fixed.

review_comments:
```
[00:00:16.188,903] <err> i2c_nrfx_twim: Need to use concatenation buffer and provided size is 
insufficient (1 + 1024 > 16). Adjust the zephyr,concat-buf-size property in the "I2C_0" node.
```

I would make it shorter.
```diff
diff --git a/drivers/i2c/i2c_nrfx_twim.c b/drivers/i2c/i2c_nrfx_twim.c
index a00d9fad00..a477f8fe57 100644
--- a/drivers/i2c/i2c_nrfx_twim.c
+++ b/drivers/i2c/i2c_nrfx_twim.c
@@ -86,13 +86,11 @@ static int i2c_nrfx_twim_transfer(const struct device *dev,
                 */
                if (concat_next || (msg_buf_used != 0)) {
                        if ((msg_buf_used + msgs[i].len) > concat_buf_size) {
-                               LOG_ERR("Need to use concatenation buffer and "
-                                       "provided size is insufficient "
-                                       "(%u + %u > %u). "
-                                       "Adjust the zephyr,concat-buf-size "
-                                       "property in the \"%s\" node.",
+                               LOG_ERR("Concatenation buffer is insufficient "
+                                       "(%u + %u > %u)",
                                        msg_buf_used, msgs[i].len,
-                                       concat_buf_size, dev->name);
+                                       concat_buf_size);
+                               LOG_ERR("Adjust the zephyr,concat-buf-size");
                                ret = -ENOSPC;
                                break;
                        }
```

Well, I wanted to give the user a clear indication what is wrong and how to solve the problem. Hence such verbose message. But the message is not supposed to occur normally, as it indicates an invalid build configuration, so I think its length should not be a problem and I'd rather keep it as it is.
